menu_options.controller: Media player source — a Music Assistant player for panels to play from
menu_options.install_firmware: Install firmware on a new ESP32-S3 panel — a browser and a USB cable

controller.title: Add a media player source
controller.description: A media player source binds one Music Assistant player, and panels play from it. It is added first, because a panel has nothing to control without one; a panel then finds it in a list. A source is not a device and Home Assistant lists it under Services rather than Devices.

install_firmware.title: Install a new panel
install_firmware.description:
A new ESP32-S3 panel is installed from a web page, over USB. No ESPHome, no YAML and no configuration file.

1. Open {installer_url} in desktop Chrome, Edge or Opera — the browser talks to the board directly, so the page has to be open on the computer the panel is plugged into.
2. Connect the panel with a USB-C data cable, press **Connect**, then **Install**.
3. Enter your Wi-Fi on the same page when the install finishes. The credentials go down the cable and are never sent anywhere.

The panel then shows a six-digit code and appears here as a discovered device by itself. Nothing else has to be added by hand.

pair.title: Pair the panel
pair.description: {name} is showing a six-digit code on its screen. Type it here first: Home Assistant hands the panel an access token of its own, and nothing else is asked until the panel has answered. Nothing has to be typed on the panel, and no identifier has to be read off it — the panel already said which one it is. A panel that announced itself over the network also said what kind of device it is and what it is called; one that did not is asking for both here.

controller_link.title: Media player source
controller_link.description: {name} is paired. It is a {profile} and draws up to {entity_limit} room entities. Choose the media player source it plays from.

new_controller.title: Choose what it plays from
new_controller.description: {name} is paired. A panel plays from a media player source and there is none yet, so pick the Music Assistant player and Home Assistant will create one. Nothing else is needed: room entities are the panel's own and are chosen on the next screen.

reauth_confirm.title: Pair the panel again
reauth_confirm.description: {name} is asking for a new access token, which happens after a tablet is wiped or an ESP32 is reflashed. Type the code it is showing. Its room entities and entity IDs stay as they are; only the token is replaced.

entities.title: Room entities
entities.description: {profile} draws one tile for every entity listed here, named as Home Assistant names it. Each list both adds and removes: an entity you clear is deleted and does not come back with the same identity. {remaining} of {entity_limit} places are free.

ha_url.title: Where is Home Assistant?
ha_url.description: Home Assistant could not work out an address to give {name}. Enter the one the panel should use on your network, for example `http://192.168.1.10:8123`. Set an internal URL under Settings → System → Network to skip this next time.

error.not_music_assistant: Select a media player provided by Music Assistant.
error.invalid_code: The pairing code is six digits.
error.token_failed: Home Assistant could not create an access token for this panel. Check the log.
error.code_mismatch: The panel is showing a different code. Read the six digits off the panel's screen again.
error.pairing_timeout: The panel did not answer. Check that it is on, on the same network, and still showing a pairing code.
error.controller_failed: Home Assistant could not create the media player source. Check the log, or add one from Add device → Media player source.
error.too_many_entities: That is more room entities than this panel can drive. Remove some before adding others.
error.invalid_url: Enter the address Home Assistant is reachable at on your network, starting with http:// or https://.
error.panel_already_paired: This panel already holds an access token. Remove it from Home Assistant, or reset the panel, before pairing it again.
error.panel_not_ready: The panel is still starting and has no code on screen yet. Wait for the six digits to appear and try again.
error.too_many_attempts: The panel has refused too many codes and has stopped accepting them for five minutes. Read the six digits off its screen and try again after that, or restart the panel.
error.panel_refused: The panel refused the request. Check the Home Assistant log and the panel's own log.

abort.already_in_progress: This panel is already waiting to be added. Finish the card that is open for it.
abort.reauth_successful: The panel will pick up its new token within a few seconds.
abort.no_panel_id: The panel did not announce an identifier and cannot be added automatically.

progress.waiting_for_panel: Waiting for {name} to answer with that code. Leave the panel on its pairing screen.

player.title: Music Assistant player
player.description: Move this source to another Music Assistant player. Every panel that plays from it follows. The integration reloads automatically.

panel_init.title: Panel options
panel_init.description: Everything {name} is configured with, on one page. It is a {profile} and draws one tile for every entity listed below, named as Home Assistant names it; {remaining} of {entity_limit} places are free. Each list both adds and removes: an entity you clear is deleted and does not come back with the same identity.

error.not_music_assistant: Select a media player provided by Music Assistant.
error.already_configured: This Music Assistant player already has a media player source.
error.too_many_entities: That is more room entities than this panel can drive. Remove some before adding others.

refresh.name: Refresh controller data
refresh.description: Refresh queue and playlist data immediately.

play_queue_item.name: Play queue item
play_queue_item.description: Start a Music Assistant queue item without replacing the queue.

panel_contract_outdated_tablet.title: {name} is running an old build
panel_contract_outdated_tablet.description:
This panel reports client contract {panel_contract}, and this version of Media Controller speaks contract {integration_contract}. The two no longer agree on what the config sensor carries, so the device ignores part of what Home Assistant sends it: the settings and the buttons on its device change nothing.

Build and deploy a new panel build on the tablet: run `clients/t560/build-tablet.cmd` and then `clients/t560/deploy-tablet.cmd` from a checkout of the repository. The full procedure is in `clients/t560/docs/BUILD_AND_INSTALL.md`, under "Update an existing installation".

This message clears itself once the panel reports the current contract.

panel_contract_outdated_firmware.title: {name} is running an old build
panel_contract_outdated_firmware.description:
This panel reports client contract {panel_contract}, and this version of Media Controller speaks contract {integration_contract}. The two no longer agree on what the config sensor carries, so the device ignores part of what Home Assistant sends it: the settings and the buttons on its device change nothing.

Install the current firmware over USB with the web installer at {installer_url}, then pair the panel again if it asks. The panel keeps its Wi-Fi credentials across an install. If this device was set up from an ESPHome package instead, run `esphome run` against your own device YAML: its `packages:` block re-downloads the maintained firmware and nothing in your configuration changes. A panel no longer appears in ESPHome Device Builder at all, because it no longer speaks the ESPHome native API.

This message clears itself once the panel reports the current contract.

panel_never_reported_tablet.title: {name} has never reported to Home Assistant
panel_never_reported_tablet.description:
This panel has not sent a single status report since it was set up, so its Battery, Screen, Page and settings entities stay unavailable and nothing Home Assistant sends it is applied. That is what a build from before the status endpoint existed does: it cannot report, and it does not read the settings and commands sent to it. This version of Media Controller speaks contract {integration_contract}.

Build and deploy a new panel build on the tablet: run `clients/t560/build-tablet.cmd` and then `clients/t560/deploy-tablet.cmd` from a checkout of the repository. The full procedure is in `clients/t560/docs/BUILD_AND_INSTALL.md`, under "Update an existing installation".

If the device is simply switched off, ignore this: it clears itself the next time the panel reports.
